sourceText: Experimental light-ion plasmas; no commercial p-B11 burning plasma established in the reviewed evidence. Exact current mixture not independently verified here.
displayText: Experimental light-ion plasmas. The exact current mixture is not publicly established; no commercial proton–boron burning plasma is demonstrated.

sourceText: August release targets Da Vinci 50 MWe operations in 2031. Later filing sequencing could not be fully reconciled; do not label this a confirmed grid date.
displayText: An August 2026 release targets 50 MWe Da Vinci operations in 2031. Later filing language leaves the sequence of milestones uncertain; 2031 is a company target, not a confirmed grid date.

sourceText: Proposed merger and debt differ from equity. The filed merger is not verified closed; the supplied convertible note and additional available facility must remain separate from historic equity totals.
displayText: Proposed merger and debt differ from equity. The merger is not verified closed. The convertible note and additional available facility are separate from historical equity financing.

sourceText: ST40 experimental hydrogen-isotope plasma; exact current campaign mixture not established in the reviewed sources.
displayText: ST40 uses experimental hydrogen-isotope plasma. The exact mixture in the current campaign is not publicly established.

sourceText: Integrate patterned magnets and liquid-metal walls into a stellarator power system; no verified current first-electricity date adopted here.
displayText: Integrate patterned magnets and liquid-metal walls into a stellarator power system. No verified current date for first electricity is included in this snapshot.

sourceText: D-D in the reviewed WHAM direct-conversion experiment
displayText: D–D in the WHAM direct-conversion experiment.

sourceText: Experimental HH70 plasma; campaign fuel details not verified in the reviewed primary releases.
displayText: Experimental HH70 plasma. Primary releases do not establish the campaign’s fuel mixture.

sourceText: UNITY engineering programme develops integrated heat-transfer and fuel-cycle testing; do not label externally heated tests as net fusion electricity.
displayText: The UNITY engineering programme develops integrated heat-transfer and fuel-cycle testing. These externally heated tests do not produce net fusion electricity.

sourceText: Business scope. Any future fission electricity must not be counted as demonstrated fusion electricity.
displayText: Business scope. A fission–fusion hybrid would draw energy from both processes. Any future electrical output would need separate accounting for the fusion contribution.

sourceText: Engineering gain; preserve the company definition when available.
displayText: Engineering gain above one is a company target for 2035. The public roadmap does not supply a complete accounting boundary for this metric.

sourceText: Fuel. Current near-term design uses DT and retains breeding/neutron challenges; older proton-boron descriptions should not be copied forward.
displayText: Fuel. The current near-term design uses D–T and retains tritium-breeding and neutron-management challenges. Earlier descriptions centered on proton–boron no longer represent this roadmap.

sourceText: Funding comparability. JPY 6 billion includes debt; do not label it equity or convert with an undocumented exchange rate.
displayText: Funding comparability. The JPY 6 billion financing figure includes debt as well as equity. It is reported here in its original currency.

sourceText: Business metrics. Radiation-testing contracts, contract-vehicle ceilings and revenue must not be charted as fusion electricity or equity funding.
displayText: Business metrics. Radiation-testing contracts, contract-vehicle ceilings and revenue measure a testing business; they establish neither fusion electricity nor equity raised.

sourceText: Experimental fuel is not specified consistently in the reviewed company releases; do not infer a D-T burn.
displayText: Company releases do not consistently specify the experimental fuel. They do not establish a D–T burn.

sourceText: RMB880m A++ round announced August 2026; earlier cumulative financing exceeded RMB2bn in May 2026. Do not display their sum as a company-reported latest total.
displayText: An RMB 880 million A++ round was announced in August 2026. An earlier cumulative figure exceeded RMB 2 billion in May. The company has not confirmed a new cumulative total combining those figures.

sourceText: Prototype plasma; exact experimental fuel not carried from reviewed partner release.
displayText: Prototype plasma. The cited partner release does not specify the experimental fuel.

sourceText: Tama Nui grid-scale plant exists as a published D-T design, not demonstrated output. No precisely dated electricity target is adopted from an undated five-year website claim.
displayText: Tama Nui is a published D–T plant design, not demonstrated output. The website’s five-year ambition is undated and cannot establish a calendar year for first electricity.

sourceText: H-mode 102 s in the same 2023–2024 campaign; do not merge metrics
displayText: H-mode sustained for 102 seconds during the 2023–2024 campaign. This is a separate result from the 48 seconds at 100 million °C ion temperature.

sourceText: Japan-Europe research tokamak supporting ITER and future power-plant plasma scenarios. Current campaign state not independently refreshed here.
displayText: Japan–Europe research tokamak supporting ITER and future power-plant plasma scenarios. This snapshot does not establish the status of its latest operating campaign.

sourceText: UW–Madison experiment with Realta; keep the university facility distinct from the company.
displayText: University of Wisconsin–Madison magnetic-mirror experiment developed with Realta. WHAM is a university facility, distinct from Realta’s proposed commercial plants.

sourceText: Cumulative amount reported with June announcement; do not silently update by arithmetic.
displayText: Cumulative financing reported with the June announcement. No later total has been inferred by adding separate announcements.

sourceText: Combined $275 million private plus $60 million government; do not add component rows again.
displayText: Combined financing: $275 million private capital plus $60 million government support. The component observations are included in this total.

sourceText: Separate Bavaria public commitment; do not treat as received equity or add to secured total.
displayText: Separate public commitment from Bavaria. This is not received equity and is excluded from the secured-financing total.

sourceText: ARPA-E SCALEUP award reported by company; do not add to private-equity series.
displayText: ARPA-E SCALEUP award reported by the company, separate from private equity financing.

sourceText: A++ completed financing; do not add to a later total that may already include it.
displayText: Completed A++ financing round. A later cumulative total could include this round; the two would not be additive.

sourceText: Announced baseline target; do not label this as commercial operation.
displayText: Announced baseline target for D–T research. ITER is an experimental facility and will not sell electricity.

sourceText: A result with hydrogen or D-D is informative but does not demonstrate D-T or p-B11 plant performance.
displayText: Experiments with hydrogen or deuterium help establish how a plasma behaves. A plant using D–T or proton–boron still needs evidence for that fuel’s reaction rates and energy losses.

sourceText: Measured reaction yield, ion/electron temperatures, radiation losses and fuel composition with uncertainty.
displayText: Fuel composition, fusion yield, ion and electron temperatures, and radiation losses, with measurement uncertainties.

sourceText: High temperature or a long pulse alone does not answer the gain question.
displayText: The fuel must be hot and dense enough, and retain its energy long enough, for fusion to compete with losses. Temperature and pulse duration alone do not establish gain.

sourceText: Simultaneous density, temperature, confinement and actual gain at a declared boundary.
displayText: Density, temperature, and energy confinement measured together, alongside fusion gain with a clearly defined measurement boundary.

sourceText: An efficient small driver or isolated subsystem may not scale to the required duty cycle.
displayText: Heating and compression systems require electricity. Their efficiency must hold at the power, pulse energy, and operating rate a plant needs.

sourceText: End-to-end electrical efficiency at required energy, power, repetition and component lifetime.
displayText: Electricity consumed versus energy delivered to the fuel, measured at the intended operating conditions and over the component’s working life.

sourceText: Energy recovered from a charged system may largely be previously supplied energy.
displayText: A thermal plant loses energy when converting heat to electricity. Direct-conversion designs also have losses; recovered electricity can include energy supplied earlier to drive the pulse.

sourceText: Measured thermal/direct conversion efficiency and full recirculating electrical ledger.
displayText: Measured conversion efficiency and a complete electrical balance, including heating, cooling, pumps, fuel processing, and changes in stored energy.

sourceText: One successful shot, high repetition at low power and full-rate high-output operation are separate results.
displayText: A pulsed design must repeat its full cycle, including fuel delivery, chamber recovery, and driver recharge where needed. A continuously operating design must sustain fusion while its supporting systems keep running.

sourceText: Long-run pulse/duty-cycle data at relevant output including failures, scheduled downtime and consumables.
displayText: Long runs at the required output and pulse rate or operating duration, including failed shots, recovery time, downtime, and consumables.

sourceText: Successful confinement can make exhaust more demanding.
displayText: Heat and particles must leave without eroding surfaces or contaminating the plasma. Cooling and exhaust systems have to work while the reactor maintains its fusion conditions.

sourceText: Integrated heat-flux control, impurity management, coolant conditions and component tests.
displayText: Heat-load and cooling measurements, impurity levels, and component tests under the intended operating conditions.

sourceText: Advanced fuel substitutes one set of constraints for another; it does not make fuel automatically free or available.
displayText: A D–T plant needs an initial tritium supply, then must breed replacement tritium from lithium and recover it fast enough to keep running. Other fuels bring different supply and processing requirements.

sourceText: Integrated mass balance, extraction/recycle rates, inventories, retention and leakage; D-T additionally net breeding.
displayText: An integrated fuel balance: supply and breeding rates, extraction and recycling times, stored inventory, material retention, and losses, including radioactive decay where relevant.

sourceText: Short discharges establish little about multiyear component life.
displayText: Neutrons can change material properties, while heat and repeated loading add stress. Component lifetimes depend on the fuel, particle energies, accumulated exposure, and operating temperature.

sourceText: Irradiation and component tests at relevant spectrum, fluence, temperature and stress, plus replacement plans.
displayText: Irradiation and component tests at relevant particle energies, exposure, temperature, and stress, with a justified lifetime estimate.

sourceText: A cheaper core can still be an expensive plant if downtime is frequent.
displayText: Worn components must be accessible for replacement. Where radiation prevents hands-on work, remote handling and the time needed to restore operation become part of the plant design.

sourceText: Demonstrated remote access, validated replacement duration, component life and waste handling.
displayText: Demonstrated access and replacement procedures, realistic outage durations, and plans for handling removed components and waste.

sourceText: A set of independently successful components does not demonstrate an integrated plant.
displayText: The reactor, power conversion, cooling, and fuel systems must work together. Component tests establish parts of that case; the complete plant still needs an operating demonstration.

sourceText: Metered complete-cycle energy balance with all auxiliaries and storage state restored, then repeat operation.
displayText: Metered net electricity over complete operating cycles, with every auxiliary load included and energy stores returned to their starting state.

sourceText: Capital raised is capacity to attempt the next milestone, not proof it can be reached.
displayText: Electricity cost depends on construction, financing, operating life, and how much time the plant actually generates. A funding announcement alone does not establish those costs.

sourceText: Cost scope, financing terms, capex, availability, lifetime, consumables, maintenance and electricity-market assumptions.
displayText: A costed plant design with explicit assumptions for construction, financing, maintenance, component replacement, fuel or targets, and operating availability.

sourceText: A lighter regulatory category reduces one burden but does not remove permitting or engineering obligations.
displayText: A proposed plant needs a site and approvals suited to its design and location. Cooling infrastructure and a grid connection must be secured as part of delivery.

sourceText: Applicable license, environmental/site approvals, cooling and grid agreements, not merely a national policy statement.
displayText: The applicable licences, environmental and site approvals, and cooling and grid agreements, with their status and remaining conditions stated.

sourceText: Unknown public evidence must be shown as unknown; company-authored peer review is not the same as replication.
displayText: A useful result identifies what was measured, how it was measured, and its uncertainty. Peer review and independent replication provide different kinds of scrutiny.

sourceText: Method, measurement boundary, uncertainty, raw/result detail, peer review and independent verification where available.
displayText: Methods, measurement boundaries, uncertainties, and enough experimental detail to assess the claim, with independent checks identified where available.

sourceText: Can the intended fuel and configuration reach useful performance?
displayText: Can the intended fuel produce enough fusion under the required conditions?

sourceText: Does the complete plant return more electricity than it consumes?
displayText: How much electricity is left after running the entire plant?

sourceText: Can the process sustain or repeat at power-plant duty?
displayText: Can the machine keep operating at the required output?

sourceText: Can the plant obtain, process and replenish fuel at its own operating rate?
displayText: Can the fuel supply keep up with operation?

sourceText: Can components survive, be replaced and permit useful availability?
displayText: How long will components last, and how long will replacement take?

sourceText: Can the complete facility be financed, built, permitted and operated economically?
displayText: What will it take to build and operate the complete plant?

sourceText: Alpha heating supports a propagating burn in an experiment yielding over 1.3 MJ; target gain remains below one.
displayText: Helium nuclei produced by fusion, called alpha particles, heat the surrounding fuel and help the fusion reaction spread. The experiment releases over 1.3 MJ of fusion energy, still less than the laser energy delivered to the target (target gain below one).

sourceText: Record listed: 8.6 MJ fusion yield from 2.08 MJ laser input; target boundary only.
displayText: Target gain 4.13 means the fusion reaction released 4.13 times the laser energy delivered to the target: 8.6 MJ from 2.08 MJ on 7 April 2025. It compares fusion energy with laser energy at the target, excluding electricity used by the lasers and the rest of the facility.
